# Tools (25 tools)

Every interface (MCP, REST, WebSocket, OpenAI format) runs these same tools under the same access policy. Unknown input is rejected. Each tool description is the text the model sees.

## Decision matrix

This table is generated from the `decide` function itself. Path rules, the allowed/denied command lists and the service list are applied separately, before it.

| Operation | `read_only` | `developer` | `operator` | `approval_required` | `autonomous` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Read | allow | allow | allow | allow | allow |
| Write a file | deny | allow | allow | approval | allow |
| Destructive write | deny | approval | approval | approval | approval |
| Run a command in the sandbox | deny | allow | allow | approval | allow |
| Run a command without the sandbox | deny | approval | allow | approval | allow |
| Destructive command | deny | approval | approval | approval | approval |
| Control a service | deny | deny | allow | approval | allow |
| Stop/disable a service | deny | deny | approval | approval | approval |
| Control Docker (with allow_docker) | deny | deny | allow | approval | allow |
| Control Docker (without allow_docker) | deny | deny | deny | deny | deny |

- "approval" means the operation does not run until a human decides.
- At the `autonomous` level, the `auto_approve_destructive` option also runs destructive operations without approval.
- The `developer` level runs commands in the sandbox; the other levels do so only when `force_sandbox` is on. So in `operator`, `approval_required` and `autonomous`, path restrictions **do not apply to shell commands** unless `force_sandbox` is used.

Default denied paths: `*/.ssh`, `*/.ssh/*`, `*/id_rsa*`, `*/id_ed25519*`, `/etc/shadow*`, `/etc/gshadow*`, `/etc/sudoers*`, `*/.aws/credentials`, `*/.git-credentials`, `*/.netrc`

## Tool list

### `execute_command`

Run a shell command on a server. Long commands continue in the background.

**Access:** command execution (exec)

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `server` | string | yes |  | Server name or id, as returned by list_servers |
| `command` | string | yes |  | Bash command line |
| `cwd` | string \| null |  | `None` | Working directory (defaults to your first writable path) |
| `timeout_seconds` | integer \| null |  | `None` |  |
| `wait_seconds` | number |  | `20` | Return early with status 'running' after this long |

### `get_command_output`

Fetch status and new output of a command started earlier.

**Access:** read; only the assistant's own commands

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `command_id` | string | yes |  |  |
| `offset` | integer |  | `0` | next_offset from the previous call |
| `wait_seconds` | number |  | `10` | Wait up to this long for the command to finish |

### `terminate_command`

Stop a running command that you started.

**Access:** stopping the assistant's own command is allowed at every level

| Input | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `command_id` | string | yes |  |  |

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `server` | string | yes |  | Server name or id, as returned by list_servers |
| `action` | `list` \| `status` \| `start` \| `stop` \| `restart` \| `reload` \| `enable` \| `disable` | yes |  |  |
| `service` | string \| null |  | `None` |  |

**Access:** status/diff/log/show/branches are reads; the rest are exec; push counts as destructive

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `server` | string | yes |  | Server name or id, as returned by list_servers |

| `path` | string |  | `'.'` | Repository directory (for clone: the directory to create) |
| `ref` | string \| null |  | `None` | Branch, tag or commit |
| `files` | array<string> |  |  | Paths for add or diff |
| `message` | string \| null |  | `None` |  |
| `url` | string \| null |  | `None` | Repository URL for clone |
| `staged` | boolean |  | `False` |  |
| `max_count` | integer |  | `30` |  |

## Common responses

- Error: `{"error": CODE, "message": ...}` (the codes are listed in [API.md](API.md)).
- Approval needed: `{"status": "approval_required", "approval_id": ...}`; after approval, repeat **the same call with the same input**. An approval is single use and is voided if the file, the grant or the environment changes.
- Long-running command: `{"command_id": ..., "status": "running", "next_offset": ...}`; continue with `get_command_output`.
